questions.q: A 95% confidence interval for mean delivery time is 50 to 54 minutes. Which statement is the correct interpretation?
options: There is a 95% probability that the true mean lies between 50 and 54 minutes
95% of deliveries take between 50 and 54 minutes
The interval comes from a method that captures the true mean in 95% of repeated samples; this interval either contains it or does not
If we sampled again, there is a 95% chance the new sample mean would be between 50 and 54
questions.why: In frequentist statistics the true mean is fixed, so the 95% describes the long-run success rate of the procedure (the fishing net). The direct probability statement belongs to a Bayesian credible interval. The interval is for the mean, not for individual deliveries, which vary far more.

questions.q: With the same data, you switch from a 95% to a 99% confidence interval. What happens?
options: The interval gets narrower, because you are more confident
Only the point estimate changes
The interval stays the same width but shifts
The interval gets wider, because the critical value grows (about 1.96 to 2.58)
questions.why: More confidence costs width: to catch the true value more often the net must be bigger. In the delivery example the 99% interval is about a third wider than the 95% one. The centre (the point estimate) does not move.

questions.q: Twelve test cars give mean range 412 km and SD 18 km. What is the 95% confidence interval for the model's average range?
questions.why: SE = 18 / √12 = 5.196 km; with 11 degrees of freedom the t critical value is 2.201, so the margin is 11.44 km. 401.8 to 422.2 uses 1.96, which is too narrow for a small sample. 372.4 to 451.6 wrongly uses the SD instead of the SE.

questions.q: In a survey, 120 of 400 random customers say they would switch provider. What is the approximate 95% confidence interval for the true share?
A survey gives a recommend rate of 42% (95% CI 38.9% to 45.1%). Last year's figure was 40%. What can you conclude?
options: This survey alone cannot show a real change: 40% is still a plausible value, but so is any value up to about 45%
The rate has definitely not changed, because 40% is inside the interval
The rate has definitely improved, because 42% is above 40%
The survey is invalid because the interval is too wide
questions.why: A value inside the interval is not ruled out, so the 2-point rise could be sampling noise. That does not prove nothing changed; the interval also includes values well above 40%. Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

questions.q: Group A's 95% CI for average spend is ₹480 to ₹520 and group B's is ₹510 to ₹550. What can you say about the difference?
options: The overlap proves there is no significant difference
Overlap alone does not settle it; build a confidence interval for the difference (or run a test), which can exclude zero even when the two intervals overlap a little
The difference must be significant because the centres differ
Confidence intervals can never be used to compare groups
questions.why: Two 95% intervals can overlap slightly while the difference is still significant at 5%, because the SE of a difference is smaller than the sum of the two SEs. The right tool is an interval for the difference itself. Different centres alone say nothing about significance.

questions.q: Delivery times have SD about 10 minutes. How many deliveries are needed for a 95% CI no wider than **±1.5 minutes**?
questions.why: n = (1.96 × 10 / 1.5)² = 13.07² = 170.7, and you always round **up**, giving 171. 170 rounds the wrong way, 14 forgets to square, and 121 uses 1.645, the 90% critical value.

questions.q: In an interview: "How is a 95% confidence interval related to a two-sided hypothesis test at the 5% level?"
options: They are unrelated tools
A 95% interval means the p-value is 0.95
The test rejects a hypothesised value exactly when that value lies outside the matching 95% interval; the interval is more informative because it shows every value that would not be rejected
The test rejects only when the hypothesised value is inside the interval
questions.why: For a matching test and interval, values outside the 95% CI are those a 5% two-sided test would reject. That is why good reports give the effect and its CI first, then the p-value. The confidence level is not a p-value.
